title: Turn it into an Android app (APK)

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
Turn the workout timer from App 3 into an Android app (APK) and install it like a real app. Again, just your phone is enough.

Tell it on your phonemerge the PRGitHub Actions builds the APKReleasesDownload and install
  • Time: 30 minutes (including waiting)
  • You need: the my-timer repository from App 3, and an Android phone
iPhones can't install APKs. On iPhone, 'Add to Home Screen' from App 2–3 is the best way. (Publishing to an app store needs a separate paid developer account)

steps.title: Know first — four words
steps.html:
APKAn Android app install file. You can install it without an app store
CapacitorA tool that wraps a web app in an Android app box. Screens and features stay the same
GitHub ActionsA robot that builds the APK for you. Normally you'd install a big program (Android Studio) on a computer; this robot does it in the cloud
SigningA stamp saying "I made this app". Updates install over the old app only with the same stamp

Earlln's EarllnCore was made exactly this way.

steps.title: Describe it on your phone and have it built
steps.html:
Claude phone app → Code → pick the repository my-timer and send this. (Claude on a computer works the same)

It creates many files and can take over 10 minutes. It keeps working even if you close the app.
steps.code: Turn this web app into an Android app (APK). Wrap it with Capacitor and name the app 'Workout timer'. Every time something is merged into main, have GitHub Actions build the APK and upload it to Releases. Use a test (debug) APK for now, and never put signing key files or passwords in the repository

check.q: Do you see that it pushed to a new branch, and a Changes count?

steps.title: If it's slow or asks you something
steps.html:
• If Claude asks for a "package name" (e.g. com.myname.timer), choose one in lowercase. It's best never to change it later.
  • If it seems stuck, open the chat and say "carry on".

steps.title: Check the PR and merge
steps.html:
Create PR → the PR on GitHub in your phone browser → Files changed.

There are dozens of files, so don't read them all. Just check these two things.

  1. There's a file that builds the APK inside .github/workflows/ (e.g. android.yml).
  2. There are no files named like .jks, .keystore or password. (Signing keys are secret)

If it's fine: Merge pull request → Confirm merge.

check.q: Did you check both and merge?

steps.title: If you see a key file, or it's confusing
steps.html:
• If you see a key file, don't merge. Tell Claude "Remove the signing key file from the repository and build a test (debug) APK."
  • If Files changed is very long, just skim the file list (file tree) at the top.

steps.title: Wait while the robot (Actions) builds the APK
steps.html:
1. my-timer repository → Actions tab.
  2. A yellow dot on the top row means it's building. Usually 5–10 minutes.
  3. When it turns into a green ✓, it's done!

Actions is free for public repositories.
steps.alt: Green ✓, yellow dot and red ✕ in the Actions tab

check.q: Did the top row turn into a green ✓?

steps.title: If you get a red ✕ (failed)
steps.html:
That's common the first time. Show Claude the error and it'll fix it.

  1. Tap the red row, tap the red step, and copy the error text or take a screenshot.
  2. Paste it into the same chat with "Actions failed".
  3. Merge the new PR and the robot builds again.

If only the upload-to-Releases step fails, ask Claude "Also check the Actions permission (contents: write)."

steps.title: Download and install
steps.html:
1. On your Android phone's browser: my-timer repository → Releases on the right (or below) → the top release.
  2. Tap the .apk file under Assets to download it.
  3. Opening the file asks whether to allow installing "unknown apps". Allow it for your browser (Chrome) just this once.
  4. Tap Install and Workout timer appears in your app list.
steps.alt: Downloading the .apk file from Assets on the Releases page

check.q: Does Workout timer open from your app list, and does the timer work?

steps.title: If installing is blocked
steps.html:
• A Play Protect warning may appear because the app isn't from the store. Tap 'Install anyway' only for your own app.
  • If Releases is empty, Actions hasn't finished or failed. See the previous step.
  • After installing, turning 'install unknown apps' back off for your browser in Settings is safer.

steps.title: Updating · sharing with others
steps.html:
Updating

Say what to change in the same chat → merge the PR → Actions finishes → download and install the new APK. The web address (Pages) updates too.

A test (debug) APK may not update in place. The robot uses a new stamp (signature) each time. If you see 'App not installed', uninstall the app and install again. (Records may be lost)

Sharing with others

For updates to install over the old app, you need your own signing key. Ask Claude "How do I switch to signing with a release key?"

  • Never put the signing key or its password in the repository; they go in GitHub's Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions.
  • If you lose the key you can't update, so keep a safe copy elsewhere.

steps.title: 🎉 App practice 4 done! A real Android app
steps.html:
The web app you built with words is now an Android app installed on your phone. You've finished the app course!

App 1Build a web app with words
App 2–3Publish with Pages, install on the home screen (iPhone and Android)
App 4APK with Capacitor + Actions (Android)

Three things to remember

  1. The Actions robot builds the APK and posts it to Releases.
  2. Before merging, check there are no key files. Signing keys go in Secrets.
  3. Don't install APKs others send you. Allow it only for your own app.
